To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) software verification results can be transferred to AC hardware, if the hardware is constrained by the set of tolerances derived from the verification run; 2) predicate abstraction can be used as a verification technology to derive tolerances for AC; and 3) hardware constraints can be checked on the hardware level, which allows to verify AC hardware designs.
(i) we can derive tolerances for AC from successful verification runs and (ii) these tolerances are valid for AC hardware designs if the hardware satisfies the derived constraints.

1) we present a novel method for determining under which conditions a verification result carries over to approximate hardware; 2) our method is applicable to a wide range of approximate hardware designs; 3) we present an efficient implementation of the presented techniques; 4) we demonstrate our method on example C programs; 5) the presented techniques can be integrated into the verification flow.

software quality assurance on approximate hardware and contributes to both software verification and hardware synthesis.
